title: the SDP parser indexes control_url at strlen()-1 without checking for the empty string, so the index wraps to SIZE_MAX
object: RTSPStream, av_mallocz(sizeof(RTSPStream)) at libavformat/rtsp.c:286 and :525 -- one allocation
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: strlen returns size_t, so strlen("") - 1 is SIZE_MAX and control_url + SIZE_MAX is, in the modular arithmetic a byte pointer obeys, control_url - 1; control_url sits at offset 28, after two pointers and three ints, so that byte is the last of interleaved_max
allocator_layer: the object IS one allocation and the crossing is interior to it. There is no inner allocator and nothing sub-allocated the crossed region, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED. Recorded explicitly because the tally is per corpus and case.json carries no nested field.
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer. RTSPStream's members up to and including control_url are declared exactly as rtsp.h has them, which is what fixes the offset the case turns on; members after control_url cannot be reached by this defect and are left out. MAX_URL_SIZE is 4096 (libavformat/internal.h:30), unreduced.
live_proof: read from the PINNED source: n9.0.1:libavformat/rtsp.c contains the FIXED form `len == 0 || rtsp_st->control_url` (1 occurrence) and the pre-fix `control_url[strlen(rtsp_st->control_url)-1]` 0 times. Two-sided. A fix-reversal.
distinguishing: the ONLY case in this corpus that crosses DOWNWARD, out of the start of a member rather than off its end. That is also why its prediction needs stating explicitly: the access completes not because the index is small but because the member's offset is non-zero, which the case asserts (member_offset=28).

spatial.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-capstone/: **NOT CAUGHT; the defect reproduced**: the sequence completed with the crossing made, which the case's own CHECKs place inside ONE allocation, so an allocation-granular bound is in bounds for it. WHAT THIS IMAGE CANNOT SEPARATE: av_malloc and av_refstruct_allocz here are the buffer-pool port's arena carve (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c), which returns an interior pointer carrying the whole metadata arena's bounds, so no per-allocation bound exists in this image at all. The completion is fixed twice over -- the case's CHECKs keep the crossing inside one struct, and the allocator would not have bounded the struct anyway -- and this run cannot tell which. It establishes that the case runs to its defect in a Capstone domain on both arms with no fault anywhere; the 'no allocation-granular bound can see it' claim rests on the CHECKs. Build note: the driver's two aligned_alloc(64, ...) arenas are compiled as malloc, because the application SDK has no aligned_alloc (musl's fallback drags a second malloc into the link); pool-allocator.c aligns every payload from its address, so nothing relies on the arena's alignment. CAPACITY: the driver takes 80 MiB of arenas (FF2_PAYLOAD_BYTES 64 MiB + FF2_META_BYTES 16 MiB), more than the plain corpora's SDKs hold, and the first run on those refused every case at the driver's own allocation check (CONTROL-FAILED 604, recorded, not scored). These rows come from an SDK pair that differs from that one ONLY in heap capacity: level0 arena 128 MiB; Sublet pool 2^27 in a 256 MiB grant.  Fixed run of the same image: VERDICT FIXED, exit 0. Arm: the level0 heap: malloc narrows the returned capability to exactly the bytes requested (CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS), and free only marks the block free. controls in the same boot: one-past-the-end write CAUGHT (cause=7 pc=0xc8f0e5b8 address=0xc8f51768), use-after-free read RETURNED, clean access RETURNED. Image ee9215a334358e80. Predicted before the run (pre-registration 60f1c5be25a5); the prediction held.

NOT YET MEASURED: this corpus has no capstone-domain runner; cases 0-2 got their reading from probe cases 40-42 of ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/security-tests, and the same seam is where these will be measured. ARENA CAVEAT, stated rather than left implicit: this corpus's driver hands the port's av_malloc ONE arena (shared/driver.c calls ff2_memory_init on an aligned_alloc) and src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26 carves it by bumping a cursor, returning a raw interior pointer and rounding every request up to 64 bytes. __builtin_capstone_cap_shrink appears only in src/capstone-domain/payload-capabilities.c:57, on pool PAYLOAD blocks. So on this harness there is NO per-allocation bound on the struct at all, and a completion here is weaker evidence than 'the bound is the whole allocation' would be. The sub-object claim does not depend on that -- the crossing is interior by construction, which the case asserts on the offsets -- but the arm must not be read as a measured per-allocation bound.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host, revocation ON: the sequence COMPLETES on both arms and each prints its own VERDICT, so the completion is a reading and not a silent pass. NOT CAUGHT. 22 of 22 arms passed, runner exit 0, with the platform controls firing in the SAME boot: cheribsd-abi reported `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1` and cheribsd-bounds reported CHERI_BOUNDARY_READY. THE REASON IS WEAKER THAN 'CHERI BOUNDS THE ALLOCATION AND THE CROSSING STAYS INSIDE', and that is stated rather than glossed: this corpus's driver hands the port's av_malloc ONE arena (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26 bumps a cursor and returns a raw interior pointer, rounding every request to 64 bytes), so there is no per-allocation bound on the struct at all on this harness. The completion shows that nothing bounded anything at this granularity, not that a bound was in force and held. The sub-object claim does not rest on the arm -- the case asserts its own offsets. This is the over-claim that was corrected on the wmem arms, written down before it could be made again. BUILD: clang -O0, purecap, linked against the port's libffmpeg-pool.a from `cmake --preset cheribsd`. -O0 IS LOAD-BEARING: a first suite built -O1 returned VERDICT INCONCLUSIVE for case 0 while the other nineteen arms passed and both controls fired, because case 0's index is a compile-time constant one past its member and clang folded the store away. Rebuilt at -O0 with nothing else changed, it reads DEFECT-REPRODUCED. Reporting the -O1 suite would have recorded a compiler artifact as a CheriBSD reading. Evidence: results/20261006-cheribsd/.

native-detect.oracle: MEASURED two-sided 2026-10-06, results/20261006-native-subobject-7/: NO ASan report, and the arm also prints the value it crossed into, so the silence is not the access failing to happen. The positive control fires in the same probe: asan-probe-7.c's 'past' arm, one uint32 past the whole allocation, reports heap-buffer-overflow and exits 1. Built -O0, which is load-bearing -- at -O1 the dead stores are optimised away and the control cannot fire. The probe allocates with plain malloc rather than the port's arena, deliberately: inside a case binary av_malloc carves one arena, so ASan could not see an allocation bound even in principle and a silence there would prove nothing. DETECTOR NOTE: the first run of this probe read as a detection on ALL arms because it grepped for the string 'AddressSanitizer' while the probe leaked, and LeakSanitizer's summary line contains that string. Keyed on heap-buffer-overflow and with the leak fixed, the reading inverts. Recorded because a positive finding from a mis-keyed check is the mirror of a clean zero.

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm reads saw=0x5a at member_offset=28 and strlen=0 -- the low byte of the interleaved_max sentinel, one byte below control_url; the fixed arm never forms the address (saw=-1). Both arms assert the offset, so the case cannot pass on a layout where control_url is first and the reading would mean something else.
